nodes.name: CFP cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of CFP (2.5 cm×4 cm) is cleaned with concentrated nitric acid, and then washed with deionized acetone, ethanol, and deionized water.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, a piece of CFP (2.5cm×4cm) is cleaned with concentrated nitric acid, and then washed with deionized acetone, ethanol, and deionized water.

nodes.name: Co precursor hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The 4 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 2 mmol urea, and 1 mmol NH4F are dissolved in 20 mL deionized water under vigorous stirring for 30 min. The cleaned CFP is immersed in the above solution, and then transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 12 h. After cooling down naturally at room temperature, the sample is then taken out and then washed by ethanol and deionized water. The CFP coated with cobalt hydroxy carbonate [Co(CO3)0.5OH·0.11H2O] precursor (named as Co/CFP) is washed by ethanol and deionized water, and dried in a 60°C oven overnight.

nodes.name: Ni hydroxide layer hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The obtained Co/CFP is immersed in 20 mL alcohol solution with 1 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 5 mmol urea, and then transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 90°C for 6 h. After cooling down, the Ni-hydroxide layer covered Co/CFP (named as Ni@Co/CFP) precursor is taken out and washed by deionized water, and then fully dried in 60°C oven.

nodes.procedure: The N-Ni5P4@CoP/CFP is finally obtained by a common phosphorization process of above-prepared Ni@Co/CFP at the temperature of 400°C for 1 h.

nodes.procedure: The N-Ni5P4/CFP is prepared in the same way as N-Ni5P4@CoP/CFP except that the Co/CFP precursor is replaced by the CFP.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peaks at 30.4°, 40.6°, 47.0°, 47.8°, 53.0° and 54.0° indexed to (200), (210), (301), (213), (214) and (220) planes of hexagonal Ni₅P₄ and peaks at 31.6°, 35.3°, 36.3°, 46.2°, 56.0° and 56.8° ascribed to (011), (200), (112), (211), (020) and (301) of orthorhombic CoP, with Ni₅P₄ peaks slightly shifted indicating N-doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks at 30.4, 40.6, 47.0, 47.8, 53.0 and 54.0° can be indexed into (200), (210), (301), (213), (214) and (220) planes of hexagonal Ni₅P₄ (PDF No. 18-0883), whereas the peaks at 31.6, 35.3, 36.3, 46.2, 56.0 and 56.8° are ascribed to the (011), (200), (112), (211), (020) and (301) of orthorhombic CoP (PDF No. 29-0497).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals nanowire array with dendritic structure, highly oriented and vertically rooted on carbon fiber with distinctive gaps between nanowires.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the nanowire array with dendritic structure could be well-retained for the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP after phosphorization treatment (Fig. 1c), which are highly oriented and vertically rooted on the carbon fiber with distinctive gaps between nanowires (Fig. 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanowire surface composed of abundant dendritic structures with irregularity in size; HAADF-STEM reveals porous structure on nanowires surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP present that the surface of the nanowire is composed of abundant dendritic structures with irregularity in size (Fig. 1e). ... Such a hierarchical porous structure could not only increase the exposure of active sites, but also contribute to fast mass transfer.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice boundary indicating tightly integrated heterointerface; fringe spacings of 2.46 Å and 1.89 Å correlated to (111) and (211) planes of CoP; interplanar spacings of 1.91 Å and 2.23 Å matched with (213) and (210) planes of Ni₅P₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) is adopted to investigate the detailed structure of the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP. As shown in Fig. 1g, an obvious lattice boundary marked with red dashed line can be observed ... the fringe spacings of 2.46 and 1.89Å can be correlated to the (111) and (211) planes of CoP ... and the interplanar spacings of 1.91 and 2.23Å can be matched with (213) and (210) planes of Ni₅P₄.

properties.description: High-resolution TEM image showing atomic lattice

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows presence of Co, Ni, P and N elements; Co concentrated in inner region, Ni and N distributed on outer dendritic layer indicating N doping in Ni₅P₄ component.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping images indicate the presence of Co, Ni, P and N elements in the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP (Fig. 1k and Fig. S5). ... The Co element is observed to be concentrated into the inner region, whereas the Ni and N elements are distributed on the outer dendritic layer, suggesting that the N is doped in the Ni₅P₄ component.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS performed on N-Ni₅P₄/CFP, CoP/CFP and N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.7/870.1 eV (Ni-P), Co 2p at 779/794.1 eV (Co-P); positive shifts in Co-P (N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP vs CoP/CFP) and Ni-N (0.5 eV shift) indicate electron transfer from CoP to N-Ni₅P₄; higher metal-P peak area in N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) is performed to investigate the chemical composition and valence state of the N-Ni₅P₄/CFP, CoP/CFP and N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP. ... It is worth noting that the binding energy of Co-P for N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP exhibits a positive shift compared to that for CoP/CFP, confirming the electrons transfer from CoP to N-Ni₅P₄ at the heterogeneous interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES: absorption edge shifts higher vs CoP (reduced Co electron density); Ni K-edge: slight high-energy shift vs NiP (increased Ni valence).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co k-edge XANES spectrum shows that the Co absorption-edge for the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP shifts to the higher energy compared with that for CoP ... For the Ni K-edge XANES spectrum, the absorption edge of N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP slightly shifts to high energy compared to that of NiP.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Co-P peak at 1.79 Å with negative shift vs CoP; Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ni-P peak at 1.76 Å broader than NiP (1.98 Å) indicating Ni-N bonds; wavelet transform confirms Ni-P coordination predominates with Ni-N contribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Co-P peak for the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP exhibits a negative shift compared to that for the reference CoP ... the Ni-P peak for N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP (1.76 Å) becomes slightly broader than that for the NiP (1.98 Å), further suggesting the formation of Ni-N bonds ... The N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP shows a maximum intensity at 6.4Å⁻¹, which is close to the NiP (7.0Å⁻¹), indicating that Ni-P coordination mode is predominated.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ sorption shows Brunauer-Emmett-Teller specific surface area of 31.77 m²g⁻¹ and average pore diameter of 7 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pore size and surface area of the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP are studied by N₂ sorption measurement (Fig. S4), in which the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area and the average pore diameter are determined to be 31.77 m²g⁻¹ and 7 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function (Φ) difference between CoP/CFP (4.66 eV) and N-Ni₅P₄/CFP (4.92 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: which are evidenced by work function (Φ) difference between CoP/CFP (4.66 eV) and N-Ni₅P₄/CFP (4.92 eV) in Fig. S10 using ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows obvious Ni-N peak shift for N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP vs N-Ni₅P₄/CFP, proving electronic interaction between N-Ni₅P₄ and CoP at interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the obvious Ni-N peak shift can be observed for the N-Ni₅P₄@CoP/CFP and N-Ni₅P₄/CFP in Raman spectra, which can also prove the presence of the electronic reciprocity between N-Ni₅P₄ and CoP at the interface (Fig. S9).
